title: Skill 18 · 写作 Skill 的通用配方：样例 — Super Individual
title_en: Skill 18 · Examples Over Rules — Super Individual

questions.question: 在写作类 Skill 里放 before/after 样例，最主要解决的是什么问题？
options: 「简洁」「别营销腔」这类形容词，人和模型理解的取值范围不同，样例把范围钉死
模型不会遵守抽象规则，只有样例才会被执行，所以规则可以整体删掉
规则写得太长会撞到行数上限，用样例替换规则可以节省篇幅
样例越多模型越不容易过拟合，因此应尽量给每条规则都配满五对 before/after 样例
questions.explanation: 样例干掉的是「形容词没有取值」这个病：一对 before/after 让「简洁」有了可比对的验收标准。它不是用来取代规则的，规则负责给禁区命名、样例负责划界；而且样例本身最占篇幅，也会带来过拟合。
questions.question_en: What is the main problem that before/after examples solve in a writing Skill?
options_en: Adjectives like "concise" or "not salesy" mean different ranges to you and the model; examples pin the range down
Models ignore abstract rules and only follow examples, so the rules can be dropped entirely
Long rule lists hit the line limit, so swapping rules for examples saves space
More examples reduce overfitting, so every rule should be filled out with five pairs
questions.explanation_en: Examples cure the problem of adjectives having no concrete value: a before/after pair turns "concise" into something you can check against. They don't replace rules—rules name the forbidden zone, examples mark its boundary—and examples are actually the bulkiest part of a Skill and carry their own overfitting risk.

questions.question: 给每对 before/after 样例后面再加一行「Changes:（这次删了开场白和二元对比）」，主要作用是什么？
options: 压缩样例的 token 占用，让 SKILL.md 正文保持在 500 行以内
把 Input/Output 这类标签换成更自然的写法，防止模型连标签一起学走
让模型学到具体改动了什么，而不是从样例里归纳出「句子越短越好」这类错误规律
给人类审稿人留下修改记录，方便日后追溯这条样例是谁写的
questions.explanation: 只给 before/after，模型可能学成「短句好」；补上 Changes: 之后，它学到的是「删的是开场白和二元对比」，样例才变得可迁移。防止标签被学走是另一条提醒，和这一行无关；这一行也只会增加而不会减少篇幅。
questions.question_en: What does adding a "Changes:" line (e.g. "removed opener and binary contrast") after each before/after pair mainly accomplish?
options_en: It cuts the token cost of examples so the SKILL.md body stays under 500 lines
It replaces literal Input/Output labels so the model doesn't copy the labels into its output
It tells the model what was actually changed, so it doesn't infer a wrong rule like "shorter is better"
It leaves an edit history for human reviewers to trace who wrote each example
questions.explanation_en: With only before/after, the model may learn "short sentences are good"; the Changes line tells it the point was removing the opener and the binary contrast, which makes the example transferable. Avoiding copied labels is a separate tip, and this line adds length rather than saving it.

questions.question: 样例的三笔代价（过拟合、token、同化）里，为什么「同化」被认为最难对付？
options: 模型只在打磨过的那几个样例上表现好，换一篇稿子就完全失效
模型会把那段 After 当天花板，交付水平停在你写样例时的水平，而且不会报错
样例会和同时挂载的其他 Skill 规则互相冲突，导致每次输出的文风都不一样、难以复现
样例占用的 token 会随对话轮数不断累积，直到撞上上下文上限
questions.explanation: 同化的意思是模型优化的就是「像那段 After」，所以不会交出比它更好的句子；半年后你进步了，它还停在旧水平，而且一切看起来正常。唯一的办法是定期换样例。「换一篇就废」说的是过拟合，那一笔用 diverse 的样例和陌生任务测试就能缓解。
questions.question_en: Of the three costs of examples (overfitting, tokens, assimilation), why is assimilation considered the hardest to deal with?
options_en: The model only does well on the few examples you polished and falls apart on a new draft
The model treats your After text as a ceiling, so output stays at the level you wrote it, with no error to warn you
Examples clash with rules from other Skills loaded at the same time, so the style shifts on every run and can't be reproduced
Example tokens accumulate with each conversation turn until they hit the context limit
questions.explanation_en: Assimilation means the model optimizes for resembling your After, so it won't produce anything better; months later you've improved but it hasn't, and nothing looks wrong. The only remedy is to rotate examples periodically. Failing on a new draft is overfitting, which diverse examples and testing on unseen tasks can mitigate.
